source/african-and-portuguese-decoloniza.summary: Ghana's independence on 6 March 1957 stands as the first in sub-Saharan Africa; 17 African countries gained independence in 1960; the Evian Accords fell on 18 March 1962, with Algerian independence following on 3 July 1962; and the Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974 led, by the end of 1975, to independence for Portugal's African colonies.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These figures rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-25 (results listed CBC News, the African Studies Centre Leiden, Britannica, EBSCO Research Starters, Wikipedia and Portugal.com); none of the pages was opened directly. One listing gave 16 African countries in 1960, and most gave 17, so the count turns on how borderline cases are treated. The summary on the end of the Portuguese empire covered its African territories only, and did not include Macau or East Timor.

source/age-of-the-solar-system-and-earth.summary: Calcium-aluminum-rich inclusions carry a date of about 4.567 billion years; Earth's own age is given as 4.54 plus or minus 0.05 billion years; and Clair Patterson's 1956 lead-isotope measurement put the age at about 4.55 billion years, drawn from the Canyon Diablo meteorite.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These figures rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-25 (results listed Science, Wikipedia, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and NASA Astrobiology); none of the pages was opened directly. The summaries note that the inclusion age marks the Solar System's earliest solids, while Earth's age marks accretion or core formation and comes out slightly younger; the two figures are not in conflict.

source/alan-turing-search-summaries.summary: Turing set out the idea of a universal machine in 1936; he did codebreaking work at Bletchley Park, where the Bombe was in operation from March 1940; he proposed the Turing test in 1950; he was convicted of gross indecency in 1952; and he received a posthumous royal pardon in 2013.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These facts rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-25 (results listed Bletchley Park, Science/AAAS, CBC News, Biography.com and Fox News); none of the pages was opened directly. One summary loosely credits Turing alone with breaking Enigma; codebreaking at Bletchley Park was a team effort, and this note says only that he worked on it.

source/ancient-americas-on-the-oval-pala.summary: This source supports the reading that the Oval Palace Tablet shows Lady Sak K'uk' offering the headdress of rulership to her son Pakal, with both figures named in the tablet's own captions.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: What this record describes is a scholarly line drawing of the relief, made by Linda Schele, rather than the eroded original stone monument, though the iconographic reading it offers is standard within Maya epigraphy.

source/ancient-civilizations-scarre-and-.summary: An overview covering early states and the archaeology of the ancient world.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This is a textbook-level survey, and its interpretations of contested sites are simplified.

source/anderson-and-westneat-2007-dunkle.summary: A linkage model of the skull yields an estimated bite force of about 4,400 N at the tip and 5,400 N at the blade edge.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This is cited from memory and was not consulted directly. The estimate assumes a larger animal than recent size revisions support, and a 2025 study argues that the skull held more cartilage than the model assumed.

source/apollo-landings-and-lunar-samples.summary: Neil Armstrong took his first step at 02:56 UTC on 21 July 1969; six crewed landings — Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17 — followed between 1969 and 1972; twelve astronauts walked on the Moon; and about 382 kilograms of lunar samples were brought home.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These facts rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-25 (results listed NASA, the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, Britannica and Space.com); none of the pages was opened directly. The 02:56 UTC time is given to the second in one summary (02:56:15); the vault records the date only.

source/archaeology-magazine-on-anatolian.summary: A small lump of iron from Kaman-Kalehoyuk, Turkey, turned up in a layer dated about 2500 to 2250 BCE, and is reported to have been made by applying fire to iron ore, possibly ore brought from elsewhere.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was fetched on 2026-09-20 with WebFetch, which returns a model-generated summary of the page rather than its raw text. It is a news report of a single find and its interpretation, not a survey, and the report itself says more comparison of ore samples is needed before the origin of iron making can be placed.

source/armenian-genocide-search-summarie.summary: The arrests of 24 April 1915, the widening of the deportations, the causes of death, the range of death-toll estimates, and the history of Turkish denial alongside international recognition.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These facts rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-20 (results listed the Holocaust Encyclopedia, Britannica, Wikipedia, EBSCO Research Starters and the Armenian National Institute); none of the pages was opened directly. The recognition count comes partly from the Armenian National Institute, an advocacy organization, so the figure of 'more than twenty countries' is approximate, and counts change over time. The death toll is estimated within a range, and no single figure is settled.

source/art-talk-artist-profiles.summary: This source supplies the biographical facts, dates, and lists of key works behind the original 53 artist notes in 03_Entities/People (tagged artist). Each of those notes carries its profile in the art_talk frontmatter field. Artists added later cite Art-Talk (Expansion Profiles) instead.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This is a compiled secondary source. Its profiles were written from Wikipedia, a handful of museum pages, and a few printed works, and have not been checked here against primary or scholarly sources. The pictures and image credits remain in Art-Talk-main/images and Art-Talk-main/data/image-credits.json; the vault notes carry text only. All 53 profiles were read in full when converting them, from 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-27, but the resulting vault notes still carry no fact_checks: their facts have been transcribed accurately from this compiled source, not independently verified against primary ones.

source/ayutthaya-kingdom-search-summarie.summary: The kingdom's founding in 1351, the various names given to it, its role in trade and its relations with France, and the fall of its capital on 7 April 1767.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These facts rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-20 (results listed Wikipedia, the New World Encyclopedia, Humanities LibreTexts and Facts and Details); none of the pages was opened directly. The summaries gave no population figures or casualty numbers for the sack, so none are recorded here. One listed page credits the Thonburi capital to Taksin, but that attribution did not appear in the summary text, and this note does not state it.

source/barboni-et-al-2017-early-formatio.summary: A lunar zircon age of 4.51 Ga: uranium-lead and lutetium-hafnium data from Apollo 14 zircons require that the Moon had formed by 4.51 Ga, within the first 60 million years of the Solar System. The paper also reviews later estimates of 4.35 to 4.42 Ga, about 150 to 200 million years after the Solar System began.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was read in full on 2026-09-26, from the Europe PMC full-text XML of the open-access copy (PMC5226643; 37,199 characters). The date of the Solar System itself, 4.5673 Ga, which the Theia note used to cite here, does not appear in this paper.

source/bengal-famine-of-1943-search-summ.summary: The range of death-toll estimates, Sen's entitlement argument, the loss of Burmese rice imports, and the criticism aimed at Churchill and the War Cabinet's discussions.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These facts rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-20 (results listed Britannica, Wikipedia, Oxford Academic, PubMed Central and news reports of a 2019 study); none of the pages was opened directly. The death toll is contested, and this note gives only the range. Assigning blame among London, Delhi, and Bengal officials is debated, and this note records only the positions found in the summaries. One listed source was a blog post and was not relied on.

source/bergstrom-et-al-2020-origins-of-p.summary: Genome sequencing of 27 ancient dogs points to a single origin distinct from any living wolf population, with a divergence estimated roughly 40,000 to 27,000 years ago.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This is cited from memory and was not consulted directly. Other ancient-wolf-genome studies have since reopened the single-versus-dual-origin question.

source/blackpast-on-the-haitian-revoluti.summary: Independence declared on 1 January 1804, with Haiti described as the first country founded by formerly enslaved people and the first nation to abolish slavery permanently.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was consulted only through web search result summaries on 2026-09-20; the page itself was not read in full. 'First to permanently abolish slavery' is a common framing, but it depends on how earlier and partial abolitions are counted (the French emancipation decree of 1794, Saint-Domingue's 1801 constitution). This should be re-verified before citing in print.

source/blackpast-on-the-sokoto-caliphate.summary: The Sokoto Caliphate's founding, its extent, and its dates.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was consulted via web search results on 2026-09-20; the page was not necessarily read in full. This should be re-verified before citing in print. Population figures for the 19th century are estimates.

source/blackpast-on-toussaint-louverture.summary: Birth in 1743, freedom gained before 1791, the 1801 constitution, arrest and deportation in 1802, and death on 7 April 1803.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was consulted via web search result summaries on 2026-09-20; the page was not read in full. This should be re-verified before citing in print.

source/bottke-and-norman-2017-the-late-h.summary: Basin ages drawn from Apollo samples cluster near 3.9 Ga, and there is debate over whether a spike in impacts actually occurred.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was consulted via web search result summaries on 2026-09-20; the page was not read in full. This should be re-verified before citing in print.

source/braddy-et-al-2008-giant-eurypteri.summary: The pincer of Jaekelopterus rhenaniae, from the Early Devonian of Germany, yields a body-size estimate of about 2.5 m.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This is cited from memory and was not consulted directly. The size estimate rests on scaling up from a fragment, and a published comment argues for a smaller animal.

source/brahmagupta-and-fibonacci-on-zero.summary: Brahmagupta set out rules for arithmetic with zero in 628 CE, and Fibonacci's Liber abaci of 1202 introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: These facts rest only on web search result summaries consulted on 2026-09-25 (results listed Britannica, MacTutor, Wikipedia and several teaching sites); none of the pages was opened directly. Brahmagupta is described as the first to give systematic rules for zero in recorded history; that is a common claim, and the summaries do not address rival early uses of zero.

source/britannica-on-abd-al-malik.summary: Abd al-Malik's reign (685-705), the Dome of the Rock, Arabic set as the administrative language, and a reform of the coinage.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was read in full on 2026-09-26 as raw text from a Wayback Machine snapshot dated 2026-05-19 of britannica.com; the snapshot may differ from the current page (8,422 characters). The page says the Dome of the Rock was built during his reign but gives no completion date; the 691 found in the notes does not appear on this page.

source/britannica-on-al-andalus.summary: The conquest of Iberia beginning in 711, the Cordoba emirate of 756 and caliphate of 929, and the fall of Granada in 1492.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was read in full on 2026-09-26 as raw text from a Wayback Machine snapshot dated 2026-09-08 of britannica.com; the snapshot may differ from the current page (27,382 characters). The page dates the battle in which Roderick was killed to 23 July 711, and gives only the year 1492 for the fall of Granada; the months of April 711 and January 1492 found in the notes do not appear on this page.

source/britannica-on-al-khwarizmi.summary: Al-Khwarizmi's work at the House of Wisdom under al-Ma'mun, the origins of the words 'algebra' and 'algorithm', and Hindu-Arabic numerals.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was read in full on 2026-09-26 as raw text from a Wayback Machine snapshot dated 2026-09-08 of britannica.com (web.archive.org answered HTTP 403 to automated requests); the snapshot may differ from the current page (6,869 characters). The earlier citation also named MacTutor, 'Al-Khwarizmi'; that page was not read here, so nothing taken from it is confirmed by this source.

source/britannica-on-angiosperm-paleobot.summary: The age of the oldest angiosperm pollen, the Hauterivian and Barremian ages of the Early Cretaceous, about 132.9 to 125 million years ago, and the 2013 report of angiosperm-like pollen of Middle Triassic age, about 247.2 to 242 million years ago, from Switzerland, which suggests an even earlier origin.

extra.title: Caveats
extra.html: This was read in full on 2026-09-26 as raw text from a Wayback Machine snapshot dated 2026-05-15 of britannica.com; the snapshot may differ from the current page (19,073 characters). The page does not give 134 million years, the figure the Flowering Plants note had used for the oldest pollen; that note now follows this page instead.
